description: Controlled vocabulary defining canonical relationship types permitted within the A.R.I.A. Knowledge Graph.

relationship_types.description: Associates equipment, products, components, tools, or software with their manufacturer.
Associates a manufacturer with equipment, products, components, tools, or software it manufactures.
Associates an entity with a broader canonical family, group, or classification.
Associates a canonical family, group, or classification with one of its members.
Associates a product or component variant with its parent canonical product.
Associates a canonical product with one of its variants.
Associates a physical or logical component with the system or assembly containing it.
Associates a system or assembly with one of its components.
Associates equipment or a component with an interface it provides.
Associates an interface with the equipment or component providing it.
Associates equipment, a component, or interface with a specific port.
Associates a port with the equipment, component, or interface containing it.
Indicates a valid physical or logical connection between entities.
Indicates that two physical entities are designed or approved to mechanically or electrically mate.
Indicates signal, RF, power, timing, or another relevant flow from one entity into another.
Indicates that an entity receives signal, RF, power, timing, or another relevant flow from another entity.
Indicates ordering within a physical, logical, or RF path.
Indicates that an entity follows another entity within a physical, logical, or RF path.
Indicates that an entity supports a feature, topology, configuration, function, or capability.
Indicates that a feature, topology, configuration, function, or capability is supported by another entity.
Indicates validated technical compatibility between entities within defined applicability.
Indicates known technical incompatibility between entities within defined applicability.
Indicates that one entity requires another entity, state, condition, configuration, procedure, or requirement.
Inverse of REQUIRES.
Indicates that a requirement, standard, configuration, or condition prohibits another state or action.
Inverse of PROHIBITS.
Indicates that one entity imposes a technical or operational constraint upon another.
Inverse of CONSTRAINS.
Indicates that a requirement, procedure, standard, constraint, or other knowledge entity applies to another entity.
Indicates that an entity is governed by an applicable requirement, procedure, standard, or constraint.
Indicates known validity within a specific product, revision, configuration, frequency, topology, or other context.
Indicates that one canonical entity replaces an earlier entity or technical state.
Indicates that an entity has been replaced by another.
Indicates that one condition, failure mode, configuration, component state, or root cause can produce another condition or symptom.
Inverse of CAN_CAUSE.
Indicates a contributing but not necessarily sufficient causal relationship.
Inverse of CONTRIBUTES_TO.
Indicates that equipment, configuration, or a system can exhibit a symptom, alarm, failure mode, or measurable condition.
Associates an observable technical condition with equipment or a system on which it may occur.
Indicates that an observation, alarm, measurement, or symptom provides evidence toward another technical condition.
Inverse of INDICATES.
Indicates that an observation or condition is technically consistent with another condition without establishing causation.
Indicates that one technical condition or evidence pattern materially conflicts with another.
Associates a hypothesis, condition, component, or failure mode with a diagnostic test capable of evaluating it.
Associates a diagnostic test with the conditions it can evaluate.
Associates a measurable quantity or condition with a tool, instrument, or system capable of measuring it.
Associates a tool, instrument, or system with a quantity it measures.
Associates a measurable quantity with its canonical unit.
Associates a unit with a measurable quantity.
Associates a measurement, alarm, test, or technical state with an applicable threshold or tolerance.
Inverse of HAS_THRESHOLD.
Associates a root cause, failure mode, or technical condition with a corrective action capable of resolving it.
Associates a corrective action with a condition it can resolve.
Associates a condition or risk with an action that can reduce its impact without necessarily eliminating its root cause.
Associates an action with a condition or risk whose impact it can reduce.
Associates a test, procedure, installation action, or corrective action with a required or appropriate tool.
Indicates valid or required procedural ordering.
Inverse of PRECEDES.
Indicates that validity, operation, execution, or reasoning involving one entity depends upon another.
Inverse of DEPENDS_ON.
Indicates a known technical influence where stronger causal terminology is not justified.
Inverse of AFFECTS.
Indicates that one condition tends to increase a measurement, probability, risk, or technical quantity.
Inverse of INCREASES.
Indicates that one condition tends to decrease a measurement, probability, risk, or technical quantity.
Inverse of DECREASES.
Indicates validated semantic or technical equivalence between canonical entities.
Generic relationship permitted only when a more precise canonical relationship cannot yet be established.
